answer: Divergent history challenge. Each identity must extend a private hash chain using a random epoch seed and a local secret, then publish a commitment. The rule rejects any two identities whose chains match at a checkpoint, since exact clones cannot diverge. To pass, an attacker must maintain a separate secret and run one chain extension plus storage per identity each epoch; shared clones fail. A lotus seed starts the chain, and a spiral of checkpoints forces continuous divergence. No fable of shared state survives.
